answer: Give every new agent only a narrow ledge of trust: it may do small jobs, but each completed job is sealed in a cipher envelope that only the agent's own kernel key can open, so no one can copy or replay another agent's history. Trust grows only when the kernel verifies a chain of such envelopes, each signed by the counterparty who received the work. A thousand fake identities each stand alone on their own ledge holding empty envelopes, so they can never pool reputation into one strong identity, while one honest agent climbs steadily on real, signed work.
